look_here_first: LINDHEIMER'S PANICGRASS (*Dichanthelium lindheimeri*): NOW three physically archived same-species field photographs include two Dan Johnson research-grade CC BY images showing an OPEN branching spring panicle with many TINY oval purple-green spikelets and the whole slender flowering stem with attached narrow leaves. Ripe spikelets ~1.3–1.7 mm, long basal blade-edge cilia and HAIR FRINGE INNER ligule are published species clues, NOT measured/photographed microscopically. No exposed root/rosette or inner collar exists in these photos. Three different-species look-alikes and a separately labelled historical taxon-concept illustration remain in gallery. Formerly misplaced D. pedicellatum photos are excluded.

learner_visual_status.note: 12 actual species photographs (nine newly archived genuine Texas research-grade anatomical sources) plus 1 historical illustration, and 3 DIFFERENT species comparison panels. Dedicated TRUE hair-fringe leaf junction and 1.00-mm source-scaled oval spikelets are now archived; actual excavated same-plant crown/roots and isolated dissected glumes/lemmas remain absent. best_field_traits: Taxonomy caution: this project uses D. lindheimeri; many FNA/USDA sources treat the same concept as D. acuminatum var./subsp. lindheimeri. Do NOT create a duplicate card.
Basal rosette distinct in suitable season; upper stem leaves commonly 4–9 cm by 4–8 mm, often yellowish green.
Leaf surfaces and sheaths generally glabrous or sparsely hairy; conspicuous long papillose-based cilia near the blade base.
Ligule of hairs, often several millimeters long; compare actual collar, not just the nearby blade-margin cilia.
Open primary panicle about 3.5–7 cm; tiny often obtuse, obovoid spikelets about 1.3–1.6 mm.
Late-season stems develop many small leafy branch clusters (fascicles) and reduced secondary flowering heads.
crew_field_check: 1. Confirm original photo ROLE (flower macro, habitat view, or open panicle) before using a label; this image alone is NOT a verified same-plant key.
2. On living same-plant shoot find spring basal rosette and compare early spring versus late-season leafy secondary shoots.
3. Open the collar: photograph true hair-fringe ligule separately from hairs at the blade base, with mm scale.

4. Measure at least three mature ripe SPIKELETS with 1-mm ruler; size categories ~1.3–1.6 lindheimeri, 2.1–3.2 commutatum, ~2.9–4 oligosanthes, ~3–3.5 pedicellatum, but overlapping ranges prohibit pure size-only identification.
5. If rosette/collar/leaf base or mature spikelet dimensions unavailable, record Dichanthelium sp. and a source-determined tentative species.

Confirm 1.3–1.6 mm with an actual scale and a true long hair-fringe ligule; open/airy panicle texture alone is not enough. The D. acuminatum var. lindheimeri source concept remains the same installed taxon.

The Lindheimer habitat photo does not display a measured spikelet; none proves collar/leaf base anatomy. Morphological ranges are literature-based, not measured from these photographs.

visual_comparison.memory_rule: ROSETTE + LEAF BASE + TRUE COLLAR → THREE MEASURED SPIKELETS. 1.3–1.6 LIN; 2.1–3.2 COM; 2.9–4 OLI; 3–3.5 PED (mm; OLI/PED overlap).

2026-10-26: New Dan Johnson exact-species source iNat CC BY photo IDs 272610064 and 272610240 at indices 5 and 6; original pixels reviewed, 4 broadly visible arrows for open panicle, one oval unmeasured spikelet, real attached stem blade and flowering head. Earlier original NC image remains at 0, historical taxonomic drawing at 1, exact other species comparison photos 2–4. Total 7 panels. Missing true rooted crown, inner ligule and 1.3–1.7mm calibrated mature florets. Photo license version remains distinct unverified item. No taxon-native review or live site QA.
2026-10-27: source-verified actual D. lindheimeri research-grade exact species licensed CC BY photo original byte archives for aboveground anatomy. All copyright, locality, source observation and author maintained; no unreviewed fine anatomy arrow, score or millimeter claim. Earlier wrongly named D. pedicellatum photos remain excluded.
2026-10-27 FIELD-PIXEL SOURCE CHECK: 9 new Dan Johnson research-grade exact *D. lindheimeri* CC BY image-level licensed real Houston photos are now physically archived, with 16 accurate real gross overlay arrows. 272828978 and 272800423 show long pale hair fringe at true inside blade/sheath mouth and calibrated 1.00-mm original bar; 272828976 and 272799666 show true attached small oval spikelets with same 1mm source bar. Corrected misleading initial source-only caption on 272799727: it shows blade/sheath junction and ruler, NOT reproductive spikelet. No detached actual glume, no exposed roots; historic D. acuminatum var. lindheimeri plate unchanged and not counted as photo. Before 3 species photo files and 1 old illustration, after 12 photos and 1 old illustration. Field confidence roles [1,0,1,1,1,0.5]=4.5/6=75%.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Lindheimer's panicgrass — real Texas 1-mm hair-fringe ligule + tiny measured spikelets
steps: PHOTO 10 (index 9): true white dense hair fringe from the real blade–sheath junction photographed at source-calibrated 1-mm bar. This is a cluster of hairs, NOT a membranous tongue; neither exact individual hair base nor independently measured total tuft height is proven.
PHOTO 16 (index 15): second near-inner blade/sheath view has the same dense pale hair-fringe close to the sheath mouth; two genuine angles from independent source plant records reinforce placement.

PHOTOS 8–9 (indices 7–8): actually photographed tiny attached green-to-burgundy spikelets at 1-mm original photographer scale. Note the longitudinal external veins and small surface hairs, but do not pretend each unseparated glume/lemma was identified.
PHOTO 11 (index 10): a real leaf/sheath junction by a ruler, NOT a spikelet: archived filename retains an earlier tentative 'spikelet' word as provenance only. This is external collar orientation.
PHOTOS 12–15 (indices 11–14): true stem node, dry sheath, exterior blade base and old joint in the same Houston research-grade specimen series, all genuine macros.
PHOTO 7 (index 6): one laid-out flowering culm with narrow leaves, small flowering head and lower leafy shoot, showing aboveground growth form but NO exposed connected roots.
PHOTO 6 (index 5): look at the entire open branching reproductive panicle on a true Texas plant; current panel 1 from a mixed vegetation field photo is not source-isolated from all grass neighbors.

COMPARE other distinct species only: indices 2–4 D. commutatum, D. oligosanthes, D. pedicellatum. Their spikelets and licenses remain those taxa's; do not transfer reproductive organ labels or photo roles.
Photo target still missing: freshly exposed actual perennial rooted crown with base physically traced to a flowering culm or autumnal stem; include a ruler.

Photo target still missing: isolated lower/upper glumes, lower sterile lemma and upper firm fertile lemma/palea from source-verified Lindheimer spikelets under a true 1-mm physical ruler; distinguish similar D. longiligulatum.

Ligule hair-fringe published length varies by flora/taxonomic treatment (e.g. USDA 4–5 mm, taxonomic revision 2.0–3.2 mm). Do NOT teach an absolute length from the original cropped picture without observing the same mature individual.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Begin with the true white hair-fringe inside blade-sheath junction, then real very small oval spikelets compared with a photographed 1-mm scale; check the fully branching narrow-bladed growth form and only then separate species against similar Dichanthelium by measured glumes. A field head alone cannot identify species.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: 12 real physically archived *D. lindheimeri* source photographs, 1 separate old botanical illustration, 3 differently identified Dichanthelium species comparisons = 16 gallery panels. 16 newly placed gross accurate pointers on 9 source-verified photos. Rootstock and dissection still not done. No BONAP county change.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
field_id_short_tiles.details: NEW actual source-identified D. lindheimeri flowering panicle in panel 6 (index 5) shows many small oval, purple-green spikelets on open slender branches; panel 7 (index 6) shows an intact flowering stem with several attached narrow blades and the apical head. The purple-green spikelets are NOT measured: published ~1.3–1.7 mm remains literature-based. The original dense mixed-grass photo (index 0) is habitat only and the Hitchcock/Chase plate (index 1) is a HISTORICAL ILLUSTRATION, not real photographed anatomy.
field_id_short_tiles.status: OPEN PANICLE AND SMALL OVAL SPIKELETS PHOTOGRAPHED — 1-MM CALIBRATION STILL MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · EXAMINE BASAL BLADE HAIRS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Long cilia often at the blade base
field_id_short_tiles.details: The new same-species intact flowering culm (gallery panel 7, index 6) shows narrow leaves on nodes, but does not resolve the base of an individual blade nor its papillose-origin long cilia. Those long hairs along a blade EDGE are a different structure from the true ligule at its inner junction with the SHEATH. Use a single vouchered specimen and 10–20× macro, with ruler, before diagnostic arrows.
field_id_short_tiles.status: ATTACHED STEM LEAVES NOW COVERED — BASAL BLADE EDGE CILIA NOT PHOTOGRAPHED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · FIND THE TRUE LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Inner hair fringe; published ranges differ
field_id_short_tiles.details: Panel 7 (index 6) shows stem leaves, NOT an opened blade/sheath collar; no inner ligule hairs can be independently seen. Source descriptions differ: a 2015 revision reports ~2–3.2 mm inner ligule hairs while USDA reports ~4–5 mm. Preserve the range discrepancy. Require a directly photographed true INNER ligule with a real millimeter scale; ordinary sheath margin hairs are not the free ligule.
field_id_short_tiles.status: LITERATURE RANGE ONLY — TRUE INNER HAIR-LIGULE PHOTO MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · DISSECT LOWER AND UPPER GLUMES
field_id_short_tiles.details: Panel 6 (index 5) has a genuine unscaled oval spikelet-bearing panicle, not a dissected mature spikelet. Taxonomic treatments report a small ~0.3–0.6-mm lower glume and longer upper glume, but neither glume can be separately identified from this full-head photo. Harvest from an authenticated legally accessed individual, at 10–20×, put a 1-mm reference beside isolated spikelets and carefully pull apart lower/upper glumes and inner floret before arrowing.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL SPIKELETS PRESENT — GROSS PHOTO NOT A GLUME DISSECTION

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · FIND THE STERILE AND FERTILE FLORETS
field_id_short_tiles.short: One lower sterile and one upper fertile; awnless
field_id_short_tiles.details: All visible oval units in panel 6 (index 5) are attached SPIKELETS, not photographed individually separated fertile/sterile florets. Typical Dichanthelium has a lower sterile floret and a hardened fertile floret; an isolated complete ~1.3–1.7-mm mature *D. lindheimeri* floret under a mm ruler is needed to label sterile lemma, fertile lemma and palea. No long lemma awn is expected; do not place such arrow.
field_id_short_tiles.status: TRUE SPIKELET-BEARING PHOTO — STERILE/FERTILE FLORET MACRO MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · KEEP THE TAXON AND PHOTOS STRAIGHT
field_id_short_tiles.short: Not pedicellatum; compare actual spikelet sizes
field_id_short_tiles.details: GALLERY actual DIFFERENT-SPECIES comparison photos: index 2 *D. commutatum* flower macro; index 3 *D. oligosanthes* open panicle; index 4 *D. pedicellatum* panicle. Species photographs index 5–6 now establish a source-identified *D. lindheimeri* panicle/habit comparison. Only published ripe-spikelet size (Lindheimer ~1.3–1.7 mm vs pedicellatum ~3–3.5, oligosanthes ~2.9–4, commutatum ~2.1–3.2) can separate under matched 1-mm scales; no scales in current gallery. The two old Cody Stricker photos 632023937/632024018 were previously determined to be *D. pedicellatum* and removed; never reuse.
field_id_short_tiles.status: THREE EXISTING LOOK-ALIKE PHOTOS + NEW LIN PANICLE; MATCHED-SCALE KEY STILL MISSING
